name: ChannelBinding model and persistent store
description:
## Context
A chat must be linkable to a WhatsApp conversation or group. The link has to survive restarts and must not pollute the chat JSON. This is the data layer every other WhatsApp task depends on.

## Objective
Define `ChannelBinding` and its per-project store.

## Steps
1. New `codx/junior/model/channel.py`:
   - `ChannelBinding`: `id`, `project_id`, `provider` (`whatsapp`), `external_type` (`group|dm`), `external_id` (WhatsApp group id or wa_id), `chat_id`, `direction` (`both|in|out`), `reply_policy` (overrides the global one), `enabled`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `meta: Dict[str, Any]` (group name, invite link, participant count...)
   - `ChannelBindingUpsert` (request body: no ids, no project — those come from URL/query).
2. New `codx/junior/channels/__init__.py` and `codx/junior/channels/store.py`:
   - Backing file `{settings.codx_path}/channels/channels.json`, `threading.Lock` around read/modify/write, atomic write (`tmp` file + `os.replace`).
   - API: `list_bindings(project_id=None)`, `get(binding_id)`, `find_by_chat(chat_id)`, `find_by_external(provider, external_id)`, `upsert(binding)`, `delete(binding_id)`, `delete_by_chat(chat_id)`.
   - Enforce one enabled binding per `(provider, external_id)` and per `chat_id` (raise `ValueError` with a readable message).
3. New `tests/channels/test_store.py`.

## Files
- codx/junior/model/channel.py (new)
- codx/junior/channels/__init__.py (new)
- codx/junior/channels/store.py (new)
- tests/channels/test_store.py (new)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Store survives a process restart and concurrent upserts (no truncated JSON).
- [ ] Duplicate `(provider, external_id)` or duplicate `chat_id` is rejected with `ValueError`.
- [ ] `find_by_external("whatsapp", <group id>)` returns the binding used by the inbound bridge.
- [ ] Unit tests cover create/update/delete/lookup and the duplicate rules.
